rv.q: Both women can live without each other and run a tortuous scale on every syllable of every song, bending notes like Uri Geller. Effort cannot be faulted – except there's way too much of it in a laborious evening pushing three hours. Our main man, Todrick Hall, even jokes that his back hurts from carrying the show.

But everyone’s here for the production, which delivers. At points, the Burlesque musical feels like a massive Magic Mike production where shimmering torsos are the main characters, but away from the sensation, there is depth; both Hall and American singer-songwriter Orfeh who plays Tess display gravitas; they command when they stand on stage alo...

If this you think this sounds like a lot, you'd be right. At times, Burlesque The Musical feels a little like The Todrick Hall Show – but when an individual is this talented, that feels absolutely fine.
And second, the excellent cast of this noisy, frantic mess of a musical are an impressive explosion of vocal and dance talent, if not so great at the acting.
